messages.content: Tell me some of the major airports in the United States.

message.content:
Here are some of the major airports in the United States, ranked by passenger traffic and importance:

| Airport | City | State | IATA Code | Notable Features |
|---------|------|-------|-----------|------------------|
| Hartsfield‑Jackson Atlanta International Airport (ATL) | Atlanta | Georgia | ATL | Largest airport in the world by passenger traffic; major hub for Delta Air Lines. |
| Los Angeles International Airport (LAX) | Los Angeles | California | LAX | Major gateway to Asia and the Pacific; hub for American Airlines and Delta. |
| Chicago O’Hare International Airport (ORD) | Chicago | Illinois | ORD | One of the busiest airports in the U.S.; hub for United Airlines and American Airlines. |
| Dallas/Fort Worth International Airport (DFW) | Dallas/Fort Worth | Texas | DFW | Hub for American Airlines; one of the largest single-site airports in the world. |
| Denver International Airport (DEN) | Denver | Colorado | DEN | Largest airport by land area in the U.S.; hub for United Airlines and Southwest. |
| John F. Kennedy International Airport (JFK) | New York City | New York | JFK | Major international gateway; hub for American Airlines and Delta. |
| San Francisco International Airport (SFO) | San Francisco | California | SFO | Major hub for United Airlines; key gateway to Asia. |
| Seattle–Tacoma International Airport (SEA) | Seattle | Washington | SEA | Hub for Alaska Airlines and a growing hub for Delta. |
| Miami International Airport (MIA) | Miami | Florida | MIA | Major hub for American Airlines; key gateway to Latin America. |
| Orlando International Airport (MCO) | Orlando | Florida | MCO | Major hub for Southwest Airlines; serves many leisure travelers. |

These airports are among the busiest in terms of passenger numbers, flight operations, and cargo throughput. They also serve as major hubs for the largest U.S. carriers and provide extensive domestic and international connections.
